data.title: Temperature
data.tagline: A parameter that adjusts sampling randomness in generation APIs and models that support it
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a lower or higher randomness direction for a task and know it cannot guarantee a fixed format.
data.description: When asking AI to name a to-do app, a higher temperature usually allows more varied wording; for a response with a fixed format, a lower setting may reduce variation. It cannot lock outputs to identical wording, and support and ranges differ by model and API.

learning.assumes: You have seen repeated runs of the same request return different wording.
learning.outcome: You can choose a lower or higher randomness direction for a task and know it cannot guarantee a fixed format.

distinctions.label: Maximum output length
distinctions.explanation: Maximum output length limits how much can be generated; temperature adjusts sampling randomness. More room does not make wording steadier.

distinctions.label: Structured output
distinctions.explanation: Temperature only affects sampling variation; JSON fields and types need a format constraint and checks on the actual result.

explanation.title: First check API support
explanation.text: For models and APIs that support it, lower values usually concentrate sampling and higher values usually add variation. Check the relevant documentation for supported ranges.

explanation.title: Constrain a required format separately
explanation.text: A low setting can still produce missing or incorrect fields. Define the structure and validate the actual output.

data.boundary: Temperature shifts the tendency of sampling variation; it does not guarantee identical sentences, correct answers, or a fixed format.

lessonPractice.title: The team asks AI to name a to-do app, but the suggestions sound alike. If the API supports temperature, what should you try first?

options.label: Raise the temperature somewhat, then compare another set of names
options.feedback: Correct. Higher temperature usually increases wording variation for exploring candidates; it does not guarantee that every result is novel or useful.

options.label: Lower the temperature so the candidate names differ more
options.feedback: Lower temperature usually concentrates sampling, which works against the goal of exploring more varied wording.

options.label: Increase the maximum output length to give the model more words
options.feedback: Output length limits how much the answer can contain; it does not directly control sampling variation.

data.agentPrompt: First check whether this model and API support temperature. Compare candidates for the same naming request at different settings, treating them as a trend in randomness rather than a guarantee that low temperature repeats every word. If the format must be fixed, define it separately and validate the result.
